sc-029.summary: In a decaying room, a dark figure at the windows turns to reveal himself as Morpheus, who welcomes Neo and sits him down. Morpheus probes why Neo has come, reframing Neo's hacker-hero worship into a deeper, felt conviction that 'something is wrong with the world.' When Neo names 'The Matrix,' Morpheus defines it as an illusory world 'pulled over your eyes' that keeps everyone 'a slave' in 'a prison for your mind,' then admits it cannot be explained, only seen. He offers Neo a final choice between a blue pill, which ends the story and returns him to comfortable ignorance, and a red pill, which means staying to learn the truth. Neo swallows the red pill, and Morpheus tells him to follow.

what_changes.before: A legendary hacker meeting his idol, expecting a straightforward encounter.
what_changes.after: Confronted with the reality that his lifelong unease points to a hidden, enslaving system he can no longer un-know.

what_changes.before: Hesitant and physically nervous about crossing an irreversible threshold.
what_changes.after: Commits to the truth, accepting there is 'no going back.'

what_changes.before: A distant, mythic figure known only by reputation.
what_changes.after: An active guide who has secured Neo as a recruit ready to be shown the truth.

minds.wants: To get Neo to name his own dissatisfaction and then commit to the truth — to convert a fan meeting into a genuine, self-chosen recruitment.
minds.feels: A controlled, patient certainty. He is not testing a hypothesis; he is executing a ritual he has done before, and the certainty is the point — he already knows Neo will say yes, so his pressure can be gentle.
minds.shows: Warmth and courtesy — 'the honor is mine,' a smile that 'lights up the room,' offering a seat. He withholds the answer ('no one can be told [...]') and stages the choice as if it were entirely Neo's.
minds.basis: He redirects Neo's hero-worship ('You're a legend') toward an internal feeling ('something is wrong with the world'), refuses to explain and instead offers a choice of pills, and says 'all I am offering is [...]' — language that frames coercion as pure non-coercion. The 'Cheshire smile' returns only after Neo commits.

believes_about.belief: That Neo has come because he already half-knows the truth and is ready to be freed — that this particular recruit is different from ordinary curiosity.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo has named a feeling, not a fact; he is acting on a lifetime of unease and on Trinity's warning, not on knowledge. Morpheus is right that Neo will say yes, but wrong about how much Neo actually understands of what 'yes' costs — which the post-choice scenes (the horror of the pod, the atrophied body, the mind rejecting the history) will correct.

believes_about.belief: That presenting the choice as pure freedom — 'nothing more' than the truth — is honest and clean.
believes_about.wrong_because: The framing ('this is your last chance,' 'no going back') is engineered persuasion dressed as neutrality; Morpheus believes he is offering an equal choice when he has already decided the red pill is the only real answer.

minds.wants: To finally know what the 'splinter in his mind' is — to stop living with the nameless wrongness — while not losing control of himself in the process.
minds.feels: Overwhelmed and physically exposed: heart pounding (carried from sc-028), moisture in his palms, swallowing hard. He is both terrified and relieved that someone authoritative finally names the thing he could not.
minds.shows: Nervous deference and attempted coolness — 'You could say that,' the legend-worship line — then a hard swallow and a nod instead of speech when asked if he wants to know. He lets the physical tremor show rather than hiding it.
minds.basis: sc-028 established 'Neo can hear his own heart pounding' and Trinity's advice 'Be honest. He knows [...],' which licenses Neo's honesty here. He answers Morpheus's probes directly, names 'The Matrix' himself, and physically reacts (swallow, damp palms) at the moment of irreversible choice.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a benevolent guide offering him genuine freedom and 'nothing more.'
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is a recruiter with a predetermined end in mind (the event shows the pill is a trace program that unplugs him); Neo does not yet know that 'the truth' will mean the loss of his body, his old life, and any return — that Morpheus has already broken a rule against freeing minds like his (ev-010).

believes_about.belief: That this is a meeting between equals where Neo is in control of his decision, consistent with his stated disbelief in fate.
believes_about.wrong_because: The entire encounter has been orchestrated — Trinity's extraction, the staged room, the scripted choice — so Neo's sense of choosing freely is itself part of what Morpheus has arranged.

minds.wants: To deliver Neo to Morpheus intact and honest, having done her part of the handoff.
minds.feels: Alert and invested — she has risked herself to bring him this far and stakes her judgment on his honesty.
minds.shows: Almost nothing here: she relays Morpheus's nod and exits through the door to the adjacent room, leaving the two men alone. Her presence is silent.
minds.basis: In sc-028 she gave Neo the advice 'Be honest. He knows [...]' and led him to room 1313; here she nods him toward the chair and leaves on Morpheus's signal, positioning herself as the trusted intermediary who has already vouched for both parties.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is worth vouching for — that his honesty will hold up in front of Morpheus.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is less a mistake than a wager; nothing in the scene contradicts it yet, but it is a belief she is staking rather than something the scene confirms.

connects_back: sc-028: Trinity's advice ('Be honest. He knows [...]') licenses Neo's direct, unguarded answers to Morpheus.
sc-028: Neo's pounding heart carries into this scene's physical nervousness (swallowing hard, damp palms) at the threshold.
The long pursuit/extraction that delivered Neo to room 1313 — he arrives already committed enough to cross the door.
sets_up: ev-006: Neo swallowing the pill as the act that lets the crew trace and unplug him from the Matrix.
ev-007 / ev-008: The irreversible 'no going back' — his body must be recovered and rebuilt because there is no return to his old life.
ev-009: The payoff of 'you have to see it [...] now owes Neo the visible truth he could not be told.
ev-010: The cost Morpheus has incurred by freeing a mind that wanted out — the rule he broke by recruiting Neo.
sc-029.dramatic_function: It converts Neo's vague, lifelong dread into a named enemy and then into an irreversible, self-chosen commitment, so that the catastrophe of unplugging feels earned rather than inflicted — the scene's job is the crossing of the threshold, not the consequences past it.

sc-012.summary: Neo is asleep in front of his PC in his technology-crammed studio apartment when the screen goes blank and a prompt appears: "Wake up, Neo." He wakes, confused, and tries to type but the keyboard types a message on its own instead: "The Matrix has you," then "Follow the white rabbit," then "Knock, knock, Neo." At that last message someone actually knocks on his door, and the screen goes blank. Neo, "still unnerved," asks who it is; it is Choi, a young Chinese man with several friends, two hours late. Neo opens the door with the chain still on, then closes it to retrieve a disk he has hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations near his bed, stuffing Choi's "two grand" into the book. He hands the disk through the crack to Choi, who calls him "my Savior, man! My own [...]!" and agrees "This never happened. You don't exist." Neo is hit by "the strange feeling of unrealness" and asks Choi if he has ever been unsure whether he is awake or dreaming; Choi jokes it is mescaline and says Neo needs to "unplug." Dujour urges that they take him out; Neo refuses because he has to work tomorrow, but when he notices a small white rabbit pin among the dozens of pins on her black leather jacket, "The ROOM TILTS" and he agrees to go: "Yeah, yeah. Sure, I'll go."

what_changes.before: Asleep and ordinary at his PC, living an unremarkable night.
what_changes.after: Shaken by an intrusion that blurs the line between the machine and reality, unable to explain it.

what_changes.before: Able to explain his world in cause-and-effect terms.
what_changes.after: Doubting whether he is awake or dreaming, and unable to articulate what just happened.

what_changes.before: Refusing to go out: "I can't. I have to work tomorrow."
what_changes.after: Committing to go with them after seeing the white rabbit pin.

objects_that_matter: the messages on the screen ("Wake up, Neo", "The Matrix has you", "Follow the white rabbit", "Knock, knock, Neo")
the door with its series of locks and chain
Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations, hollowed out to hide computer disks
Dujour's black leather motorcycle jacket and its pins
uncertain: Whether the on-screen messages are sent by a real external party or are a hallucination.
Whether Neo's "feeling of unrealness" is caused by the messages, exhaustion, or something else.
Whether Dujour's white rabbit pin is a deliberate signal meant for Neo or a coincidence he interprets as one.

minds.wants: To complete the illegal disk-for-cash deal cleanly and get Choi away from his door without exposure, while privately wanting to know whether the on-screen messages were real.
minds.feels: Genuinely shaken. The machine behaved as if it had a mind of its own and then a knock answered the last message; this has cracked his ability to trust cause-and-effect. Beneath the routine of the deal runs a current of dread and a dawning sense that his ordinary hacker's life is not as solid as it looked.
minds.shows: A competent, guarded black-marketeer: multiple locks, door-chain discipline, a hidden hollowed-out book, a brisk 'You're two hours late / You got the money?' He performs normalcy so completely that when he tries to name what happened he can only ask Choi if he's ever been unsure he's awake. He then commits to going out on the strength of a pin.
minds.basis: He flips 'a series of locks [...]' — deliberate concealment and control. He hides the disk in a hollowed Baudrillard and only retrieves it after securing the money, showing a practiced criminal routine. After the deal he 'nods as the strange feeling [...]' and, 'unable to explain what just happened,' asks Choi, 'You ever have the feeling [...]?' He refuses to go out ('I have to work tomorrow') until he sees the white rabbit pin, at which 'The ROOM TILTS' and he agrees.

believes_about.other: the on-screen messages / whoever sent them
believes_about.belief: That they are either a hack or a glitch he can file under 'weird night,' not a message with intent directed at him.
believes_about.wrong_because: The event shape and the following scenes establish that 'Trinity' accessed his computer and is deliberately steering him — the messages are an external summons, not a malfunction, and he is the target, not a bystander.

believes_about.other: the white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket
believes_about.belief: That it is a coincidence he happens to notice, which is why agreeing to go feels impulsive and unaccountable.
believes_about.wrong_because: The pin is the literal fulfillment of 'Follow the white rabbit' — a planted breadcrumb on the exact person sent to collect him. He reads it as chance precisely because he does not yet know he is being guided.

believes_about.belief: That Choi is merely a drug-buying customer whose 'Savior / Jesus Christ' line is just stoner gratitude, and that 'You don't exist' is a throwaway reassurance about the deal.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has no idea how literally true 'You don't exist' is — that his entire identity in this world is a fabrication he is about to be unplugged from. The customer's flippant line is accidentally prophetic.

believes_about.belief: That his 'feeling of unrealness' might just be exhaustion or something he can joke away, since he still frames it as a question.
believes_about.wrong_because: The feeling is the first edge of the truth he will spend the film confronting — that his ordinary world is not real — and treating it as a passing mood lets him keep functioning while the ground drops out.

minds.wants: To get the disk and get out, while flattering his supplier so the pipeline stays open.
minds.feels: Buoyant and insulated — he has his 'two grand' worth of contraband and treats the whole transaction, including Neo's rattled state, as a lark. He is not interested in Neo's inner life except as material for a joke.
minds.shows: Loud, grateful, and glib: 'Hallelujah! You are my Savior [...]!' then, when Neo goes pale, he diagnoses it as mescaline and recommends he 'unplug' — a line that lands as stoner wisdom but, to the audience, as literal truth he cannot possibly mean.
minds.basis: He hands over the envelope ('Two grand'), erupts in messianic praise, and on seeing Neo 'a little whiter than usual' deflects into a joke ('It's called mescaline and it [...]') before slapping his friend's hand and floating the idea of taking Neo out. He also reassures Neo unprompted: 'This never happened. You don't exist.'

believes_about.belief: That Neo is just a slightly paranoid, over-caffeinated hacker who needs to relax and party, and that his pale, dreamy demeanor is a drug effect or fatigue.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is not high or tired — he has just been contacted by people who will soon reveal his world is a simulation. Choi's comic misread is the last 'normal' interpretation Neo will receive before everything changes.

believes_about.belief: That this is a clean, forgettable black-market exchange protected by the code 'This never happened. You don't exist.'
believes_about.wrong_because: Within this same night Neo will be pulled out of that world entirely; the phrase Choi uses as criminal slang is about to become Neo's literal condition.

minds.wants: To pull Neo out of his apartment and into the night — the specific errand of the people who sent the messages.
minds.feels: Purposeful and unbothered; she is the instrument of 'Follow the white rabbit' and applies light, friendly pressure ('Come on. It'll be fun. I promise') rather than force, knowing the bait on her own jacket will do the work.
minds.shows: Casual enthusiasm — she agrees instantly ('Definitely') and reassures him, reading his hesitation as ordinary reluctance about work rather than the vertigo of a man whose reality just glitched. She never reveals that she is, in effect, the rabbit.
minds.basis: She is the one Choi consults ('What do you think, Dujour [...]?'), answers 'Definitely,' and, when Neo refuses on the grounds of work, presses with 'Come on. It'll be fun. I promise.' Her jacket carries 'dozens of pins' including the small white rabbit that, the moment Neo notices it, makes 'The ROOM TILTS' and flips his answer to 'Sure, I'll go.'

believes_about.belief: That he is a mark to be coaxed out with the promise of a good time, and that his reluctance is mundane.
believes_about.wrong_because: She does not know — and the scene doesn't show her knowing — that Neo is 'The One' the whole operation is built around; to her he is simply the guy on the list they've been told to collect.

connects_back: sc-011 establishes that the Agents now have the name 'Neo' and a search is running — this scene opens on Neo asleep and ignorant of it, so his rattled but ordinary night is shadowed by a manhunt he doesn't know he's at the center of.

sc-009–011 show Trinity escaping the Agents after being warned of the target; the cryptic messages that wake Neo are the off-screen continuation of that same cell's effort to reach him before the Agents do.

The 'informant is real' line in sc-011 (the search began on the strength of a real contact) is what makes Neo's willingness to complete a black-market deal and then follow a stranger's instructions legible as him already being in motion toward the resistance.
sets_up: ev-002: Neo going out with Choi and Dujour puts him in the club where Trinity will approach him, confirm she was behind his computer, and pose 'What is the Matrix?'
ev-002/ev-003: Neo's 'I have to work tomorrow' and his fragile grip on routine set up the next-morning lateness and Rhineheart's reprimand that precede the Agents' capture of him.
ev-006: Neo's willingness to 'unplug' (Choi's joke he half-accepts) and his growing doubt about whether he is awake foreshadow his choice of the red pill and his physical unplugging from the Matrix.
The 'You don't exist' exchange and the 'Savior / Jesus Christ' framing seed the claim, delivered in ev-004, that Neo is 'The One.'
sc-012.dramatic_function: To move Neo out of passive, asleep-and-ordinary isolation and into active motion toward the resistance by blurring the boundary between the digital and the real — the screen 'types back,' a knock answers the screen, and a planted symbol (the white rabbit) converts a drug deal into an abduction-by-invitation — so that the audience, and Neo, begin to distrust the solidity of his world just as the Agents close in on his name.

sc-024.summary: The car carrying Neo moves through a dark, wet urban environment: 'the green street lights curve [...].' The scene is a brief transitional shot of the vehicle in motion, with no dialogue and no other visible characters.

what_changes.before: Stationary beside the open car door on the bridge, deciding whether to get in.
what_changes.after: In the moving car, rushing through the 'wet underworld,' committed to whatever lies ahead.
